properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check (comparing every 'trusted' parcel's committed pixel bbox against a fresh color-detected bbox) found this block's committed shape only ~110px wide against the diagram's real ~180px width, and extended noticeably too far south. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [105,64,115], '50ft Max') in a tight crop, connected-component labeled it, and extracted its precise contour (OpenCV) -- a clean pentagon (a rectangle with its SE corner cut at an angle) at pixel (1677,734), (1677,907), (1757,907), (1857,883), (1857,734). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. New area (~0.71 acres) is noticeably larger than the old (wrong, narrow) trace. Confirmed zero overlap with E1, E3, or the waterfront open space corridor; still overlaps Elevation Sky Park by ~1133 m2 (an already-documented, expected overlap given ESP's own low-confidence placement -- see that file). CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (found via join_approximate.py's new MAJOR CLIP warning, prompted by user-flagged issues elsewhere): confirmed via direct satellite comparison that this block's north edge sits on real, currently-paved road pavement (a real street/driveway visible with clear edges near the shoreline), not vacant land -- 37% of this block's area was inside the buffered real-street layer. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer, same pattern already used for Parcels D/E1/H1/H2; area dropped from ~2,883 to ~1,807 sq m.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Designated use is 'Arts' per both the D4D (excluded from the developer's standard parcel-purchase option as 'the arts building parcel') and Brookfield's own leasing brochure -- NOT residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category; treat the real designation as Arts. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
